item.title: Human: Fall Flat Achievements Guide - All 151 Steam Achievements (2026)
item.description:
Human: Fall Flat Achievements Guide (All 151 in 2026)

Steam lists 151 achievements for Human: Fall Flat: 51 in the base game plus 100 across 25 DLC levels. A base-game 100% run takes 15–20 hours; full DLC completion runs about 46 hours. This page breaks down each category and gives unlock routes, including the three 0.1% rarity hidden achievements.

1. Stat-grind Achievements (Auto-accumulate)

These unlock through natural play; no targeted grinding required, but knowing the conditions prevents missing them:

  • Tourist (travel 1km) — held by 79.3% of players, unlocks through normal play.
  • Traveler (travel 10km) — accumulates across multiple runs.
  • Adventurer (travel 25km) — long-term players get this naturally.
  • Trampoline (jump 1000 times) — accumulates through normal play.
  • Climber (climb 100m) — cumulative climbing height; long walls help.
  • Heavy lifting (carry 1000m) — cumulative carry distance; planks across whole levels contribute most.
  • Let it rain (respawn 100 times) — fall off ledges repeatedly.
  • Learn to swim (drown 10 times) — triggered by staying underwater in the Water level.

2. Base Level Completion Achievements (10)

Each base level grants one completion achievement, in order of appearance:

  • Leap of Fail — complete Mansion
  • Choo Choo! — complete Train
  • Don’t Get a Splinter! — complete Carry
  • What Goes Up — complete Mountain
  • Brute Force — complete Demolition
  • Storm the Gate! — complete Castle
  • Feet First / Head First — complete Water diving feet-first and head-first, in two separate runs of the same level
  • The End? — complete Power Plant
  • The End — complete Aztec
  • It’s Alive! — complete Dark

For full walkthroughs of each level see the 30-Level Walkthrough Index.

3. Base Game Hidden Achievements (rarer)

These don’t unlock from completion alone — you must perform specific actions inside each level:

  • Mind the gap! — take a large shortcut in Mansion.
  • Public service — place 5 pieces of debris in a dumpster in Carry.
  • Perfectionist — align a flipped bench with a wall.
  • It’s stuck — jam a door and go through it in Carry.
  • Tower — stack all 4 boxes in Carry.
  • Pigeon Simulator — stand on the head of the statue in the intro.
  • Surprise! (Avalanche!) — unleash the boulder gate in Demolition.
  • Wrong direction — use the window on the left instead of smashing the wall in Demolition.
  • Primal — break 4 walls without using any gadgets in Demolition.
  • Improvised Ammo — launch yourself with the catapult in Castle.
  • For whom the bell tolls — ring the castle bell in Castle.
  • Zipline — zipline from the church tower in Castle.
  • Smooth moves — parkour fluidly from alley to blacksmith in Castle without touching ground.
  • Row, row, row your boat — use the row boat to reach the cargo ship in Water.
  • Reverse gear — enter the dock with the ship backwards in Water.
  • Beacon — light up the lighthouse in Water.
  • Breathing exercise — get out of water in 100ms to avoid drowning in Water.
  • Surfer — surf down the mountain without getting wet in Water.
  • Electricity 101 / Will it fry? / Thief / Delivery boy — Power Plant’s electrical puzzle achievement chain.
  • Bird’s eye view / Rollin’ / Clockwork — Aztec’s hidden paths and pendulum challenge.
  • Tick Tock / Planks? No Thanks! — Dark’s clock tower timing and bridge challenges.

4. Rarest Achievements (0.1% — the three hardest)

These are the rarest, hardest achievements in the game:

  • Cheaters never prosper — destroy the cheat sheet rune in the Viking level. Requires finding the hidden rune deep in the level and destroying it in a specific way.
  • Practice makes perfect — hit all dummies with a sword in Viking. Requires completing every dummy hit in sequence without missing.
  • Let off some steam — find and turn all hidden valves in Steampunk Party.

Full solutions for these three live on the Viking walkthrough and Steampunk walkthrough pages.

5. Speedrun Achievement

  • Speedrun — complete the entire game start-to-end in a single run. No world-record time is required, but you can’t exit a level back to the main menu mid-run. Build familiarity with the shortest route per level first; see Physics Glitch Guide for engine exploits that shorten paths.

6. DLC Achievements (100, across 25 DLC levels)

Beyond the base game, 25 DLC levels (Christmas, Power Plant, Water expansion, Castle expansion, Aztec expansion, Dark expansion, Viking, Steampunk Party, Candy Land, Golf, Forest, Lighthouse, Copper World, and more) each carry roughly four achievements: complete the level plus collect hidden items.

Representative DLC achievements:

  • Top the Hat — stand atop the large snowman’s hat in Christmas
  • Bah, Humbug! — shoot the Christmas angel off the tree top
  • Deck the Halls — land in the snow fort in Christmas on a snowboard
  • Candy Rush — zipline down from the mountain in Christmas using a candy cane

DLC achievement logic mirrors the base game: complete the main path first, then revisit for hidden items. Each DLC level has a dedicated page in the Level Index.

7. Recommended Completion Route

If you’re aiming for 100%:

  1. Solo-clear the 10 base levels — this naturally grants completion achievements and most stat achievements.
  2. Revisit for base hidden achievements using the “Hidden items” section of each level page.
  3. Tackle the base Speedrun achievement once you know each shortest route.
  4. Clear each DLC level, doing hidden items alongside.
  5. Finish with the three 0.1% rarity achievements, which need targeted practice.

For movement mechanics see Core Physics Tricks Guide, and for speedrun-friendly glitches see Physics Glitch Guide.

item.title: Human: Fall Flat Beginner FAQ - 8 Common Questions Answered
item.description:
Human: Fall Flat Beginner FAQ

Almost everyone who first launches Human: Fall Flat watches Bob’s wobbly body and assumes the controls are broken. This page answers the 8 most-asked beginner questions so you can start climbing walls and having fun.

1. Why is Bob so wobbly? Is it a bug?

It’s not a bug — it’s the design. Bob is a soft-body physics character. Every movement is simulated live by the physics engine: arms, torso, and legs all obey inertia and gravity. The “wobble” you see is the engine solving each joint in real time.

The soft body gives extreme freedom of motion — you can hang one-handed from a cliff edge, hug a rolling ball, wedge your body into a narrow gap. The trade-off is that Bob won’t respond to inputs with the precision of a traditional action game. Learning to work with the physics engine instead of against it is lesson one.

2. How do I grab things? What are the controls?

Grab is split into independent left and right hand controls:

  • Keyboard + mouse: left mouse button controls the left hand, right mouse button controls the right hand. Hold to grab, release to let go.
  • Gamepad: left trigger (LT) controls the left hand, right trigger (RT) controls the right hand. Hold to grab.
  • Hold both grab buttons: both hands grab simultaneously — essential for wall climbing, ledges, and carrying large objects.

For the full control map and advanced moves see Basic Controls Guide.

3. Why can’t I climb walls?

Wall climbing is the core skill in Human: Fall Flat, and every newcomer fails it on the first try. Three key points:

  1. Alternate hands — don’t hold both buttons and slide down. One hand grabs and holds still, the other moves up to a higher position and grabs, then release the lower hand, repeat. This is the “monkey climbing” motion.
  2. Lean forward — if you only grab without moving your body, gravity pulls Bob off. Tilt Bob’s torso toward the wall and let friction hold you in place.
  3. Don’t go straight up — diagonal walls are far easier than vertical ones. If a slanted surface is available, take it.

Detailed movement mechanics (swinging, throwing, vertical climbing, climb-jump) live in the Core Physics Tricks Guide.

4. Is there fall damage?

No. Bob takes no damage from any fall (the game has no health system). Falling just sends you back to the last checkpoint. Jump freely from heights — it’s one of the most useful exploration tools.

The only “lethal” mechanic is underwater breath in the Water level — staying submerged too long “drowns” you and sends you back to a checkpoint. Even then, you don’t truly die; you return to the last save point.

5. How do checkpoints work? Does the game auto-save?

Each level has multiple checkpoints (typically glowing circular zones) that activate when you pass through them. Dying or falling out of a level returns you to the most recently activated checkpoint.

Progress is auto-saved: entering a new level, activating a checkpoint, and completing a level all trigger autosave. No manual saving needed. Next time you launch the game, you can jump straight to any unlocked level from the main menu’s level select.

6. How do levels unlock? Do I have to go in order?

Base levels unlock in sequence — completing one makes the next available on the main menu. But shortcuts exist: each level has multiple paths, and some allow special jumps to trigger later level entrances early (this isn’t cheating; it’s a physics-engine-sanctioned solution).

DLC levels are clickable on the main menu as soon as you buy or pick them up — no need to clear the base game first. Steam Workshop community levels require subscribing to the corresponding Workshop item before you can play them.

7. Keyboard or controller — which is better?

Strong recommendation: controller. Independent hand grabs feel far more natural on triggers than on mouse buttons, and long wall-climbing sessions are noticeably less tiring. The game fully supports Xbox and PlayStation gamepads, and Steam natively supports both.

Keyboard + mouse is playable — speedrunners even use it for finer control — but controllers give beginners a smoother ride.

8. Solo or co-op? Does multiplayer affect completion?

Solo play can fully complete every base and DLC level — multiplayer is not required. Co-op simply widens the solution space — eight-player teams can stack human ladders, split carrying duties, and relay-throw items, but every puzzle is solvable solo.

The appeal of co-op is the physics engine’s chaos amplifier: eight Bobs crammed into one elevator, grabbing the wrong person and tumbling off a cliff together, lobbing a friend over a wall like a baseball — only multiplayer delivers these moments. For the co-op setup walkthrough see How to Play with Friends.

item.title: Basic Controls Guide
item.description:
🎮 Basic Controls Guide

In Human: Fall Flat, Bob’s wobbly body has two independently controlled arms. Every keyboard/mouse input is converted into torque output for his wobbly muscles. This guide will help you build muscle memory and master the fundamental movement physics.

📸 Basic Climb: Grab the ledge with both hands, look down, and pull yourself up.

⌨️ Input Command Terminal

Familiarize yourself with the default key bindings to coordinate Bob’s limbs:

  • Move Walk: Use WASD.
  • Rotate Head/View: Move your Mouse. Bob’s hands reach toward the center of your crosshair.
  • Left Grab: Hold Left Mouse Button. Left hand sticks to the target.
  • Right Grab: Hold Right Mouse Button. Right hand sticks to the target.
  • Jump: Press Space. Jumping carries forward momentum when moving.
  • Run: Hold Shift. Bob bends over slightly and accelerates.

📐 Mechanics & Core Movement Systems

1. Grab & Release System

  • The Physics: As long as you hold down the Left/Right Click, Bob’s hands act as high-strength sticky pads. Any surface (walls, boxes, teammates) will be stuck tight.
  • Tip: Release the mouse buttons to let go. When carrying objects, keep the hands flat and pull backwards to slide items smoothly.

2. Standard Wall Climb (Step-by-Step)

This is the most critical hurdle for new players. Master this 4-step sequence:

  1. Approach & Look Up: Move up to the wall, look straight up at the sky, and raise both hands high.
  2. Jump & Grab: Press Space to jump. Ensure both hands stick to the top ledge of the wall. Keep holding the mouse buttons!
  3. Pull Up (Look Down): Slowly move your mouse down to look at the ground. Bob will naturally pull his torso up to the ledge.
  4. Forward Over: While looking down, press and hold W. Bob will swing his legs over and climb on top.
【Climbing Tip for Beginners】
Many beginners fail because they release the mouse buttons too early when trying to step onto the ledge. Remember: Never release your mouse clicks until both feet are firmly on top of the wall! Keep looking down until Bob climbs over.

For advanced physics engines techniques, check out our Core Physics Tricks Guide.

item.title: Community Speedrun & Physics Glitches Guide
item.description:
🚀 Community Speedrun & Physics Glitches Guide

While the developers intended Human: Fall Flat to be a slow-paced puzzle platformer, the game’s wobbly physics engine holds secrets that speedrunners have exploited for years. By exploiting collision math, frame-rate physics ticks, and arm stretch limits, you can fly across maps and climb infinite vertical walls.

This guide details the top four community techniques used to break the game’s boundaries.

📸 Glitched Climb: Defying gravity by exploiting Bob's arm-rotation friction physics.

🧗 1. Vertical Flap / Paddling (左右划水爬墙法)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
  • Purpose: Climb completely smooth, flat vertical walls to infinite heights.
  • Theory: When Bob grabs a wall and rotates his camera, the shoulder joint stretches. By alternating left and right grabs while rotating the camera rapidly, you bypass the vertical limit.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Stand facing the wall. Raise both hands and jump to grab as high as you can.
    2. Release your Right Hand only.
    3. Quickly flick your mouse to the right (about 45–60 degrees). This rotates Bob’s hips and shoulder, raising his free right arm higher up the wall.
    4. Grab the wall with your Right Hand at this new height.
    5. Release your Left Hand. Flick your mouse to the left.
    6. Grab the wall with your Left Hand at the new height.
    7. Repeat this rhythm: Release Right -> Turn Right -> Grab Right -> Release Left -> Turn Left -> Grab Left. It will look like Bob is “paddling” or “flapping” up the wall.

🪂 2. Single-Hand Super Swing (单手极限摆荡)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆
  • Purpose: Swing across massive gaps using a single anchor point, gaining double the normal momentum.
  • Theory: Grabbing with both hands distributes weight evenly but limits swing range. Grabbing with only one hand allows Bob to act as an offset pendulum, creating torque.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Jump toward the swing rope, pipe, or ring, and grab it with only one hand (e.g., Left Hand).
    2. Hold down the forward movement key (W) as you swing forward.
    3. When you reach the peak of the forward swing, do not release. Instead, turn your camera 90 degrees away from the swing direction and press A or D to slide Bob’s body around the rope.
    4. Swing back, and then swing forward again. On the second forward swing, press the keys to twist Bob’s body.
    5. The twisting motion adds rotational velocity. Release the grab at the peak of the second swing to propel yourself twice as far as a normal two-handed swing.

🏹 3. Slingshot Glide / Zipline Inertia (吊索势能惯性弹射)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
  • Purpose: Launch yourself across the map when releasing from ziplines, cables, or swinging chains.
  • Theory: If you release a grab while Bob’s body is stretched to its limit, the physics engine releases the elastic tension instantly. This converts hook tension into pure forward velocity.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Grab a zipline handle or rope.
    2. Slide down to gain speed. As you near the end of the line, hold back (S) to pull your body behind the hook, stretching Bob’s arms.
    3. Suddenly release S and press W. Bob’s body will snap forward like a rubber band.
    4. Release the mouse clicks at the exact microsecond Bob’s body passes directly under the hook.
    5. If timed correctly, the velocity will double, gliding you hundreds of meters in the air.

🖥️ 4. FPS Checkpoint Skip (帧率调节逃课)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆
  • Purpose: Force Bob to glitch through solid metal gates or skip checkpoint triggers.
  • Theory: Human: Fall Flat calculates collision detection based on frame rate. At extremely high or low frame rates, the physics engine’s tick rate changes, allowing Bob’s wobbly limbs to clip through solid meshes when squeezed.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Go to a door or gate with a small gap (like the iron gates in Castle or Dark).
    2. Squeeze Bob’s body sideways into the corner where the gate hinges meet the wall.
    3. Grab the wall inside the gap with both hands and pull hard.
    4. FPS Manipulation: Speedrunners use keybinds or settings to temporarily cap their FPS to 15 (creates physics lag) or unlock it to 300+ (creates high-frequency collision updates).
    5. Wiggle your camera left and right rapidly. The collision solver will fail to calculate Bob’s boundaries in time, popping you straight through to the other side of the gate.

📊 Speedrun Glitch Matrix

Glitch Technique Difficulty Best Maps to Use Approximate Time Saved
Vertical Paddling ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ Mountain, Aztec, Castle 3 - 5 Minutes per map
Single-Hand Swing ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Mansion, Steam, Water 1 - 2 Minutes per map
Slingshot Glide ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Dark, Thermal, Port 2 - 3 Minutes per map
FPS Checkpoint Skip ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Castle, Dark, Power 4 - 6 Minutes per map
⚠️ Warning: Glitch climbing and FPS manipulation take hours of practice to master. Start by practicing "Vertical Paddling" on the flat walls in the starting courtyard of Level 1: Mansion.

Want to apply these glitches? Read our Mansion Walkthrough or choose a level from the Level Guides Index to find skips!

item.title: Core Physics Tricks Guide
item.description:
💪 Core Physics Tricks Guide

Once you master basic grabs, you can unlock Bob’s inertia engine. By combining coordinate rotations and friction limits, you can perform advanced movements that bypass standard puzzles entirely.

📸 Swing Jump: Converting gravitational potential energy into forward speed.

🎛️ Training Modules: Advanced Physics Guides

1. The Swing Jump (Pendulum Action)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐☆☆☆
  • Application: Crossing super-wide chasms using ropes, poles, or hanging lanterns.
  • Action Sequence:
    1. Jump and grab the rope/lantern at the highest possible point.
    2. Hold W and S in cycles. Push forward at the peak of the backward swing, and pull back at the peak of the forward swing to build momentum.
    3. Once the swing reaches maximum speed, wait until you reach the highest point of the forward arc (when speed drops to zero for an instant).
    4. Release both grabs instantly, and press Space to launch yourself forward.

2. Single-Hand Wall Climb (Horizontal Wiggle)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
  • Application: Climbing flat vertical walls without any ledges.
  • Action Sequence:
    1. Face the wall, raise one hand (e.g. left hand) and grab it. Leave the other hand free.
    2. Swing your camera to the right, raising the free right hand above the left hand. Grab the wall with your right hand.
    3. Release the left hand click. Swing your camera to the left, raising the left hand above the right hand, and grab.
    4. Repeat this coordinate rotation back and forth to walk your hands up the wall.

🏆 Physics Training Matrix

Trick Name Difficulty Core Mechanism Training Map Recommendation
Swing Jump ⭐⭐☆☆☆ Gravity & Pendulum Swing Mountain, Castle
Glitch Throwing ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Inertia & Torque Release Carry, Factory
Single-Hand Climb ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ Coordinate Wiggling & Friction Mansion, Mountain
Super Jump ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Frame-Rate Collision Glitch Any flat ground
💡 Tip for Glitch Climb: Always make sure your camera is rotated at least 45 degrees sideways when raising the free hand. This forces Bob's shoulder joints to stretch higher than normal, allowing you to reach further up the wall.

Ready to test your training? Head over to our Level Guides Index to check all 30 official maps!
